parsed.summary: The paper introduces SMem, a transformer architecture designed for exact memory composition, deletion, and reuse by encoding blocks independently. SMem achieves comparable perplexity to standard transformers while enabling efficient memory operations and retrieval beyond trained context lengths. It also demonstrates advantages in serving cached contexts and deletion operations, though it has limitations in pretraining requirements and recipe sensitivity.

chk_problem.value: Transformer KV cache limits exact reuse and deletion due to prefix entanglement.
chk_problem.paper_quote: The KV cache of a transformer entangles every token’s representation with its entire prefix: a passage encoded once cannot be reused under a different prefix, and cannot be removed without recomputing everything after it.

chk_method.value: SMem architecture with block-local encoding and cross-attention reader.
chk_method.paper_quote: We propose SMem (static memory: a block’s rows never change once encoded). Context is split into blocks; an encoder with block-local attention maps each block to memory rows independently of every other block; generation conditions on the union of memory rows through cross-attention (Figure 1).

chk_data.value: FineWeb-Edu dataset, 3.2B tokens at 160M scale, 8.2B tokens at 410M scale, 30B tokens at 1.5B scale.
chk_data.paper_quote: SMem and a standard pre-LN transformer are pretrained from scratch on FineWeb-Edu (Penedo et al., 2024) (GPT-2 tokenizer, T =1024, b=64, B=16) at ≈20:1 token budgets (Hoffmann et al., 2022): 160M/3.2B tokens (3 seeds per arm), 410M/8.2B (2 seeds), 1.4B/30B (1 seed; we write “1.5B” for the 1.42B-parameter scale).

chk_setup.value: Pretraining with matched parameters and token budgets, validation on held-out FineWeb-Edu data.
chk_setup.paper_quote: Validation: the last 200M tokens of the deterministic corpus stream, held out from training; each seed evaluates a fixed 0.5M-token sample of it shared across arms.

chk_primary_result.value: SMem retrieves exact-match accuracy 0.14–0.28 at distances 31 and 63 blocks at 4× trained length.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: At 4× the training length, SMem retrieves with exact-match accuracy 0.14–0.28 at distances 31 and 63 blocks across scales, beyond any window of the trained length (0.13–0.26 at distance 15, which a window reaches; primary harness; Figure 3 shows the conditional-gain view), while the learned-position transformer reads 0.00–0.02.

chk_secondary_result.value: SMem serves cached contexts at near-constant cost, reducing TTFT by 67–69% at training length.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Its cost is near-constant at 3.1–6.2 ms per request across context lengths (the pass is O(bn) in cross-attention, linear in context, against the full pass’s O(n2 ); the flatness is the launch-bound regime), while the model’s own cold prefill grows with context (Figure 2b): a 67–69% time-to-first-token (TTFT) reduction at training length and, mechanically, more at longer contexts (88–94% at 4–8×).

chk_baseline.value: Compared against learned-position transformer, RoPE transformer, and Block-Attention arm.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: At 4× the training length, SMem retrieves with exact-match accuracy 0.14–0.28 at distances 31 and 63 blocks across scales, beyond any window of the trained length (0.13–0.26 at distance 15, which a window reaches; primary harness; Figure 3 shows the conditional-gain view), while the learned-position transformer reads 0.00–0.02.

chk_conclusion.value: SMem achieves comparable perplexity to transformers and enables exact memory operations.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: An architecture that encodes blocks independently and pays for cross-block conditioning at read time reaches perplexity comparable to a parameter-matched transformer’s at every scale-and-recipe pair we ran, and gains a cache that composes and deletes exactly, serves cached contexts at near-constant cost, and, under the shared recipe, retrieves beyond the trained length where our transformer variants do not; reuse carries no approximation error to bound.

chk_limitation.value: SMem requires pretraining and has recipe sensitivity; retrieval signal weakens under tuned recipe.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: SMem is a pretraining-time choice, not a retrofit. The perplexity gap to the matched transformer spans −4.7% to +2.8%; the RoPE transformer leads all arms, and the composite that closes 29–59% of the distance to it has a single seed at 410M and none at 1.5B; evidence at 1.5B is a single seed pair under Regime 1, and under the tuned recipe the far-range exact-match signal sits near the floor (§3.2), so a deployment that tunes for perplexity should not assume it.
